chunks: Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abi al-Mughira from Talha ibn Zayd from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) passed by a people who were crying. He asked, 'What is making these people cry?' It was said, 'They are crying over their sins.' He said, 'Let them give them up, and they will be forgiven.'

key_terms.عِیسَى ابْنُ مَرْیَمَ: Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary)

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Isa say to people crying over their sins?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, Prophet Isa (AS) observes a group weeping over their sins and advises them to cease the sins themselves, implying that true repentance requires action rather than mere lamentation. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tawbah* as an active process of abandoning the sin, where divine mercy is contingent upon the cessation of the transgression. The incident underscores the accessibility of God's forgiveness for those who genuinely turn away from their wrongdoings.
